speakers: Katie Kaminski (co-host, trend following researcher and portfolio manager)
Neils Kostrup Larsen (host, hedge fund manager)
summary: November 2025 Systematic Investor recap: trends working again after a tough H1 (Liberation Day three-day turbulence shock), precious metals and equities leading, short-term traders lagging. Kaminski stresses parameter robustness and combining methods, discusses AQR-style economic trend, total portfolio approach, alternatives growth and managed futures for target-retirement worst cases.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: despite whatever it was, 40 days of no government data, the markets didn't really seem to be too bothered about that
claims.claim: Markets barely reacted to 40 days without official US economic data, questioning how much investors need routine data releases.
claims.testable: partly - one episode (Oct to Nov 2025 shutdown)

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: the only truth is the market price because that's where the market is caring
claims.claim: Price data is the pure, hard-to-manipulate signal, whereas official economic data can be delayed, manipulated or missing, which weakens economic-trend signals.
claims.direction: prefer price trend over economic data signals
claims.conditions: small commodity markets may be manipulable
claims.testable: partly - robustness comparison of economic vs price signals

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the line item problem and sort of this subdivision of labor in the investment management creates this very siloed view
claims.claim: Bucket-by-bucket optimisation misses total-portfolio effects; under a total portfolio approach, trend following's total-portfolio risk reduction (locally vs globally optimal) should raise its allocation.
claims.indicator: trend following allocation under total portfolio approach (CalPERS vote)
claims.conditions: institutional adoption of total portfolio approach

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: they completely stopped using anything to do with buckets
claims.claim: The Hawaii pension fund stopped using asset buckets and evaluated investments individually for portfolio contribution.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: 26% of total electricity supply in Virginia is consumed by data centers
claims.claim: AI data centres drive large electricity demand (US 183 TWh, expected to double in 4 to 5 years; 26% of Virginia supply), making electricity prices a plausible new inflation source.
claims.indicator: data-centre power demand and electricity prices

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: trend falling does really well in high inflation and rising inflation
claims.claim: Trend following performs well in high and rising inflation.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: we don't care so much about the level of inflation but we care that it's not stable
claims.claim: The worst CTA period was 2000 to 2019 with low and stable inflation, while Dunn's best compounding came in 1982 to 2000 with low but unstable inflation, so inflation instability matters more than level.
claims.testable: yes - trend returns by inflation-volatility regime

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: the total equity fund flow in in percentage of assets and it compares this year week by week uh with uh the average
claims.claim: Deutsche Bank data show 2025 equity fund inflows far above the 2010-2024 weekly average, supporting the equity trend until politicians disrupt it.
claims.indicator: equity fund flows % of assets vs 2010-2024 median

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: October had a couple of days in in in in October. The first couple of days of October was actually a little bit soft
claims.claim: October 2025 started soft but trend followers re-aligned with longer-term trends: equities, precious metals, softs mixed, currencies recovering, fixed income the main challenge.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the market wants cuts, especially for the US, but they're waiting for them
claims.claim: Fixed income trends were hard because the market wants US cuts but they are not delivered, though risk in the asset class may now be lower.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: it looks a little bit like a hedge right so you know you want the equities but if you're worried you buy the safe asset
claims.claim: Precious metals surged as a hedge alongside equities with a weak dollar, possibly aided by central banks.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: Silver is up 73% this year. Platinum 68% and gold 59%
claims.claim: By mid-November 2025 silver was up 73%, platinum 68% and gold 59% while orange juice was down 65%, showing why commodities belong in trend portfolios.
claims.indicator: gold, silver, platinum, orange juice YTD

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: the only down year uh was in 2023 where it lost 1.85%
claims.claim: BTOP50 was up in five of the last six years, with the only loss in 2023 (-1.85%), and about +2.59% YTD at 11 Nov 2025; SG CTA -0.35% and SG Trend +0.86% YTD; trend barometer 57.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, trend barometer

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: The only real lagard I find which is surprising to me is the short-term traders index
claims.claim: The SG Short-Term Traders index lagged in 2025 (down 4.8% vol-adjusted) despite short-term corrections, because of event-risk whipsaws and frequency mismatch.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: having sort of ironically like just a very long-term view this year in some asset classes would have been very helpful
claims.claim: In 2025 a very long-term view that ignored early-year noise (e.g. in equities) helped, while faster systems traded whipsaws.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: it's really sort of the robustness of those parameter choices that matter to me the most
claims.claim: Judge strategies primarily by out-of-sample performance and by how stable statistics remain when parameters are permuted, because overfitting the past is easy; then also look at downside/upside capture and Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: you should do a little bit of most of those things
claims.claim: Combine parameter schools (fixed vs dynamic, recent vs long data, per-market vs common) rather than rely on one view.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: adjust those parameters over time, things like machine learning
claims.claim: Advanced or machine-learning parameter adaptation may add some value over classic moving-average rules, but the past may not resemble the present (e.g. bonds under a divided Fed).

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: some markets react more quickly than other markets
claims.claim: Market elasticity (reaction speed) differs by market and might inform per-market trend parameters, without overoptimising.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: Why is it completely opaque to the world how these strategies are are because they are so big in size
claims.claim: Bank QIS and similar systematic strategies are larger than official CTA assets yet opaque, so regulation to disclose them is suggested.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: Q1 and Q2 were very challenging. Q3 and Q4 have been much better
claims.claim: Trend followers struggled in H1 2025 after the Liberation Day shock (erratic, headline-driven price discovery before macro changed) and improved in H2 as calmer markets showed consistent trends.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: turbulent days so like high magnitude surprise days
claims.claim: Turbulent (high magnitude surprise) days are very negative for CTAs, which usually recover the next day or so.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: liberation day was actually three days in a row
claims.claim: Liberation Day was the first time in the studied history that magnitude surprise lasted three consecutive days, a sustained shock that is hard for trend systems because it is not in the backtest.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: it also begs the question of like examining how you measure your volatility and how it reacts to a much more sustained shock
claims.claim: Recent events should not change the model, but they raise questions about how volatility estimates and signals respond to sustained shocks.
claims.indicator: volatility estimate response to sustained shocks
claims.testable: yes - stress test of vol estimator

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: not just using price data for their trend models
claims.claim: AQR coped well in 2025 by combining price trend with economic trend (50/50 in one program) and single-name equities, while headline risk caused chaos in price trends.
claims.indicator: economic trend plus price trend, AQR

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: if you stepped back and perhaps followed the fundamentals and looked at sort of what the overall themes of the economy were, you know, you might have sifted through some of that noise
claims.claim: In headline-driven 2025, economic trend filtered noise and worked well; but macro indicators can also predict a trend that never occurs, so trend capture of economic models must be measured.
claims.indicator: economic trend / macro indicators vs price trend
claims.testable: yes - measure trend capture of economic trend

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: macro and we have a paper coming that we've been working on on macro trading it has a very high correlation with trend falling
claims.claim: Many macro managers' returns correlate highly with trend following because both capture global trends across asset classes by different entry methods.
claims.testable: yes - correlation of macro index to trend

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: we don't try to predict
claims.claim: Pure trend following does not predict, and cannot anticipate, because it needs price data and time to adjust; economic trend feels more predictive and every approach (e.g. systematic macro IPM) has sunshine and lean periods.
claims.indicator: predictive economic data vs price trend

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: in times of stress you know often times the fundamentals become irrelevant right and so it's really about the world changing and prices are changing
claims.claim: Trend's convexity shows in the worst equity quintiles (crisis alpha): in stress fundamentals matter less than price changes, while in calm positive-fundamental years like 2025 (S&P +16%) economic trend can win.
claims.indicator: SG Trend returns by equity quintile

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: depending on the investor combining them can make sense
claims.claim: Combining price trend and economic/macro strategies depends on investor mandate: risk-mitigation investors use trend for its stress behaviour and accept modest results in strong equity years.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: from the current $4 trillion or so invested. um all the way to about $12 trillion by 2034
claims.claim: A Capgemini article projects alternatives rising from about $4 trillion to $12 trillion by 2034 (Everest Group sees $30 trillion by 2030), with high-net-worth investors at 20 to 25% and family offices at 30 to 50% allocation.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: there's never been a white paper written to suggest uh the opposite
claims.claim: Fiduciaries giving trend zero or 1% allocation are hard to justify since no paper argues trend fails to add value to a portfolio, and the shift toward private wealth access may raise allocations.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: Access is a function of both new products and new legislation
claims.claim: Private wealth and model-portfolio investors are gaining access to alternatives through ETFs and new products as concern over 60/40 grows.
claims.indicator: access to alternatives for private wealth

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: having some trend falling or managed futures of any type actually gets you farther than you would think
claims.claim: Adding even some managed futures to stocks and bonds improves diversification more than expected because it is one of the few genuinely different return sources.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: if you know your clients and you can actually reach out and talk to them um you can avoid a lot of uh unnecessary uh hardship on their side
claims.claim: Knowing the end client lets managers prevent mistimed allocation decisions after bad stretches such as Q2 2025; ETF flows hide the investor identity.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: managed futures can improve some of the down you know the worst case scenarios or some of the sort of bottom 5%
claims.claim: In a model of target-retirement cash flows, managed futures improve the worst-case (bottom 5%) outcomes caused by poor timing of allocations or withdrawals.
claims.indicator: managed futures in target retirement portfolios

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: trend falling especially with equities has a naturally you know more diversified approach and it has lower maximum draw downs on average
claims.claim: Because individuals experience one sample path, managed futures' reduction of maximum drawdown in equity-heavy portfolios helps avoid retiring into a crash like 2008 (market down 60%).
claims.indicator: maximum drawdown reduction by managed futures
